batch_notes: All four targets are Rust #[test]s wrapping Hegel::new(|tc| ...).run(); every property carries stateful_hint: true but none is a stateful model (the hint is a false positive for this shape; steel's shared Engine across cases is incidental, not an op-sequence model). Recurring rubric gaps: (1) rune's four literal round trips encode with Rust std formatting or a test-written escaper and decode with the library, so they are not 'by the same library'; classified roundtrip (name/doc lead with it, and render-then-eval is identity) but spec-postcondition ('expected answer known by construction') is an equally defensible reading. (2) Overflow-must-be-an-Err pins (rune/1, rune/2) have no clean home: the assertion is 'an error, not a panic or a silent wrap', which is neither invalid input (rejection) nor merely no-crash (robustness); filed under rejection. (3) Bignum/rational oracles from the num crates (steel) are external crates but the rubric lists bignum arithmetic under model-oracle; classified model-oracle, noting steel itself uses num-rational internally. (4) Several pins here are written as bounded Hegel properties (generators::just, test_cases(2), tiny ranges) rather than plain example tests, so they are tagged pin rather than counted as example pins. (5) Several non-pin properties gate around known bugs with tc.reject/assume or depth caps (rune arithmetic, const eval, nested expressions; steel display/read, nested source; rustybuzz shape_never_panics), which is how the two unattributed abort bugs (rune/3, steel/4) were attributed. Quality: steel's README 'What is tested' says '(no hegel tests found?)' despite 15 properties in crates/steel-core/tests/testbench.rs, and rune's README lists only the derive_from_value round trips (which are not in this batch) and none of the 14 properties here; both READMEs need regeneration. jj contributes a single property to this batch; the rest of its README-listed properties presumably sit in another batch.
